definitions.explanation: Lowering something or someone in rank, status, rating, or classification. Used in business, finance, sports, and general contexts.

examples.japanese: {信用|しんよう}{格付|かくづ}けが{格下|かくさ}げされた。
{成績|せいせき}{不振|ふしん}で{二軍|にぐん}に{格下|かくさ}げになった。
examples.english: Due to poor performance, he was demoted to the second team.

examples.japanese: {大型|おおがた}の{台風|たいふう}が{熱帯|ねったい}{低気圧|ていきあつ}に{格下|かくさ}げされた。
examples.english: The large typhoon was downgraded to a tropical depression.

examples.japanese: {部長|ぶちょう}から{課長|かちょう}への{格下|かくさ}げは、{社内|しゃない}で{大|おお}きな{話題|わだい}になった。
examples.english: The demotion from department head to section chief became a big topic within the company.

notes:
A noun used with する ({格下|かくさ}げする) or in passive ({格下|かくさ}げされる). Common in financial news (credit rating downgrades), sports (team relegation), weather reports (storm reclassification), and workplace settings (demotions).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {格下|かくさ}げする: to downgrade
- {格下|かくさ}げされる: to be downgraded
- {格付|かくづ}けの{格下|かくさ}げ: a rating downgrade
- {格下|かくさ}げ{処分|しょぶん}: demotion as a disciplinary measure

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {降格|こうかく}: demotion (focuses on rank/position, especially in organizations)
- {格上|かくあ}げ: upgrade, promotion (the opposite)
- {左遷|させん}: being transferred to a lesser post (implies punishment or sidelining)
